entries.meaning: Every file is checked for what it really holds. A picture in a .txt, .json or .md file is refused, and so is a .png that holds a DDS, a .dds that holds a PNG, and any JPEG, GIF or WebP.
entries.fix: Save each picture as a real .dds or .png, with the extension that matches its format.

entries.title: A PNG with animation or app data
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: "art.png" holds a acTL chunk, which a picture in a mod may not carry (an animation frame or app data). Export it again as a plain PNG.
"art.png" holds more than 64 KB of metadata. Export it again without metadata.

entries.meaning: A PNG in a mod is a plain picture. Animation frames, data in extra chunks and more than a little metadata are refused, because hidden data would go unreviewed.
entries.fix: Export the picture again as a plain PNG with "save metadata" switched off. That covers EXIF, XMP, comments and the colour profile.

entries.title: A texture format the game cannot load
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: "textures/a.dds" is not a DDS file.
"textures/a.dds" is a DDS format the game can't load (DXT3). Save it as BC7, DXT1, DXT5 or uncompressed 32-bit RGBA.
"textures/a.dds" is cut short.
"art.png" is not a PNG we can read.

entries.meaning: A .dds must be BC7, DXT1 (BC1), DXT5 (BC3) or uncompressed 32-bit RGBA, and a .png must be a normal PNG. Other formats and damaged files are refused, because the game would skip them.
entries.fix: Export again as BC7, DXT5 or uncompressed RGBA 8888, with no mipmaps.

entries.title: Developer mode needs the game page
where: Settings, Mods, Developer, "Load a mod you are making" (?moddev=1)

page: no developer-mode mod is running in this session
site: Start the game first: developer mode loads a mod into the running game page.

entries.fix: Press Play and wait for the title screen or your town. Then choose the folder or press Connect again.

entries.title: The folder fails playac-mod check
where: Settings, Mods, Developer, "Load a mod you are making" (?moddev=1)

site: Not loaded: the folder fails playac-mod check: mod.json: "id" is missing
Not reloaded: the folder fails playac-mod check: shops.json: a price must be a whole number of Bells, 1 to 99999

entries.meaning: `playac-mod dev` checks the folder on every save and sends nothing while the check fails. The game keeps the last good copy.
entries.fix: Fix what the message names. The terminal running `playac-mod dev` shows it too. The reload happens by itself once the check passes.

entries.title: Restart the game to load this change
where: Settings, Mods, Developer, "Load a mod you are making" (?moddev=1)
the Mod log in Settings, Mods

page: mod.json changed: restart the game to load it
site: mod.json changed: restart the game to load it.
The script cannot reload: it was not in mod.json at boot. Restart the game.
Textures cannot reload: the mod had no textures folder at boot. Restart the game.

entries.meaning: Lines, the shop, talk, letters, the calendar, the items file, the script and textures reload while you play. A change to mod.json waits for a restart, because the game reads mod.json once, when it starts.
entries.fix: Choose Restart now in the Developer section. Save your town first.

entries.title: The folder could not be read
where: Settings, Mods, Developer, "Load a mod you are making" (?moddev=1)

page: no files
"main.lua" is not file bytes
site: The folder could not be read: the folder has more than 2000 files
Stopped watching the folder: The requested file could not be read

entries.meaning: The browser could not read the folder, or the folder holds more than a mod may. The browser loses a folder when its permission ends, or when the folder is moved or renamed.
entries.fix: Choose the folder again. Pick the folder that holds mod.json, not a parent of it. Hidden files and node_modules are skipped, and everything else in it counts.

entries.title: That is not a playac-mod dev address
where: Settings, Mods, Developer, "Load a mod you are making" (?moddev=1)

site: Use the address playac-mod dev prints: http://localhost and a port.

entries.meaning: The game only talks to `playac-mod dev` on your own computer, over http on localhost or 127.0.0.1.
entries.fix: Paste the address `playac-mod dev` prints, for example http://127.0.0.1:2604.

entries.title: playac-mod dev refused this site
where: Settings, Mods, Developer, "Load a mod you are making" (?moddev=1)

site: The dev server could not be reached at http://127.0.0.1:2604: the dev server refused this site: start it with --origin https://my-copy.example

entries.meaning: `playac-mod dev` answers only playaconline.com, the dev site dev.animalcrossingonline.com and localhost:5173, so another website cannot read your folder. This copy of the game is on another address. The terminal also prints the --origin to add.
entries.fix: Start it with --origin and the address of the game page, for example `playac-mod dev --origin https://my-copy.example`.

entries.title: playac-mod dev and the game are different versions
where: Settings, Mods, Developer, "Load a mod you are making" (?moddev=1)

site: The dev server could not be reached at http://127.0.0.1:2604: the dev server speaks protocol 2; this game reads 1. Update one of them

entries.meaning: The tool and the game changed how they talk, and these two are different versions.
entries.fix: Update the tool by running its install line again (https://playaconline.com/modding/testing/#cli). Or reload the game to get the newest one.

entries.title: A file did not match its hash
where: Settings, Mods, Developer, "Load a mod you are making" (?moddev=1)

site: Not reloaded: "main.lua" from the dev server does not match its hash in the index twice in a row, so nothing was loaded: restart playac-mod dev, or choose the folder instead
The dev server could not be reached at http://127.0.0.1:2604: the dev server's index gives no sha256 for "mod.json", so its bytes cannot be checked (is it playac-mod dev?)

entries.meaning: The game checks every file from `playac-mod dev` against the hash the tool lists for it. The file did not match twice in a row, so nothing was loaded.
entries.fix: Stop and start `playac-mod dev`, then Connect again. If it keeps happening, choose the folder instead.

entries.title: playac-mod dev could not be reached
where: Settings, Mods, Developer, "Load a mod you are making" (?moddev=1)

site: The dev server could not be reached at http://127.0.0.1:2604: Failed to fetch
The dev server could not be reached at http://127.0.0.1:2604: the dev server answered 404 for /__playac/index (is it playac-mod dev?)

entries.meaning: Nothing answered at that address, or what answered is not `playac-mod dev`. Safari stops a secure page from reaching http on your computer.
entries.fix: Run `playac-mod dev` in your mod folder and use the address it prints. Use Chrome, Edge or Firefox, or choose the folder instead.

entries.title: A change was not reloaded
where: Settings, Mods, Developer, "Load a mod you are making" (?moddev=1)
the Mod log in Settings, Mods

site: Not reloaded: the game refused it
Not loaded: the stored copy does not match its id

entries.meaning: Developer mode checks every save by the same rules as installing a ZIP. A file that breaks one is not loaded, and the game keeps running the last good copy.
entries.fix: Fix the file the message names and save again. When the message names a rule, that rule has its own entry on this page.

entries.title: Visits are off in developer mode
where: the Multiplayer panel, when a visit is refused
Settings, Mods, Developer, "Load a mod you are making" (?moddev=1)

site: A mod is loaded in developer mode, so friend visits are off: no other town has that mod. Unload it in Settings, Mods, then restart the game.

entries.meaning: A mod loaded in developer mode is not installed and no other town has it, so friend visits are off.
entries.fix: Unload it in Settings, Mods, Developer, then restart the game.

entries.title: Sharing is off in developer mode
where: Share a mod, when you upload

site: Sharing is off while a mod is loaded in developer mode. Pack the folder into a ZIP (playac-mod pack) and upload that, so what is reviewed is exactly what players get.

entries.meaning: What you share must be the exact ZIP players will get, not a folder still changing.
entries.fix: Run `playac-mod pack`, unload the developer copy, restart, and upload the ZIP.

entries.title: A texture file was left out
where: the Mod log in Settings, Mods
Mods tab, on the mod's row after a restart

game: texture textures/grass.jpg not read: only .dds and .png files in the textures folder are textures
texture textures/grass.dds not read: the name is not a texture name (tex1_WxH_hash[_palette]_fmt.dds or .png)
texture textures/tex1_32x32_626709d910129694_193ca5974976e36e_8.dds could not be read: not a DDS this browser can draw (BC7, BC1, BC3 or RGBA)

entries.meaning: The game reads only .dds and .png files in the textures folder that carry a texture name, like tex1_64x64_hash_14. It skips anything else there.
entries.fix: Name the file after the texture it replaces. The model viewer copies the name for you. Save it as .dds (BC7, BC1, BC3 or uncompressed RGBA) or .png, then reload.

entries.title: Your browser cleared your mods
where: the Mods tab

site: Your browser cleared your mods. Browsers can delete a site's stored data, for example when the device is low on space or the site has not been visited for a while. Install them again below.

entries.meaning: Installed mods live in the browser's site storage, and the browser deleted it. This happens when the device is low on space, or in Safari after 7 days without a visit.
entries.fix: Install the mods again from Browse mods or from your ZIPs. Keep your own mod ZIPs somewhere safe.

entries.title: The game stopped responding with mods on
where: the Mods tab

site: The game stopped responding the last time it started with this mod on: Tea Stall. It started without mods this time. Your mods are still installed.

entries.meaning: The game stopped responding with these mods on, so this start ran once without them. One start that froze is enough. A freeze or crash later, during play, counts the second time in a row. The model viewer loads mods too, and the same rules watch it, so a viewer that froze as it started counts as well. Nothing was switched off or removed.
entries.fix: If you installed it, switch the named mod off, or one of them at a time, then restart. If you made it, test the mod alone. The usual causes are a script that does heavy work at start and textures too big for the device. A phone has 24 MB for all mods.

entries.title: Your mods could not be read
where: the Mods tab

site: Your mods could not be read: The operation is insecure.

entries.meaning: The browser would not open its site storage, where mods are kept. Private windows and blocked site data do this.
entries.fix: Use a normal window, not a private one. Allow site data for playaconline.com, then reload.

entries.title: The mods database could not be used
where: the Mods tab
Settings, Mods, Developer, "Load a mod you are making" (?moddev=1)

page: the mods database is held open by another tab
the developer mods database is held open by another tab
the mods database refused the change

entries.meaning: The browser's mod storage refused the change. Another tab of the game is updating it, or the browser stopped the write because storage is full or site data is blocked.
entries.fix: Close the game's other tabs, reload and try again. If it keeps happening, free some space on the device or allow site data for playaconline.com.

entries.title: That mod is not installed
where: the Mods tab

page: that mod is not installed

entries.meaning: That mod is no longer installed. Another tab removed it.
entries.fix: Reload the Mods tab to see your mods as they are now.

entries.title: Too many mods for one export
where: the Mods tab

page: Your mods are 600 MB together, more than the 512 MB one export can hold. Remove the mods you do not use, then export again

entries.meaning: "Export my mods" makes one ZIP in the browser's memory, and your installed mods together are more than it can hold.
entries.fix: Remove the mods you do not use and export again. Each mod is also its own ZIP, which you can get from the mod list or from its author.

entries.title: Not enough room in the browser
where: Mods tab, when you install a ZIP

page: There is not enough room in this browser's storage for this mod: it needs about 40 MB and about 12 MB is free. Remove a mod you do not use or free some space on this device, then try again

entries.meaning: Mods are kept in the browser's site storage, and it is full or blocked. A private window and switched-off site data both block it.
entries.fix: Remove a mod you do not use, free space on the device, or allow site data for playaconline.com. Private windows have very little room.

entries.title: More than 32 mods on
where: Mods tab, when you install a ZIP
Mods tab, on the mod's row after a restart

page: only the first 32 mods load
You already have 32 mods on, the most the game loads. Turn one off first
game: only the first 32 mods load; not loaded

entries.meaning: The game loads at most 32 switched-on mods. The message shows on each mod that was left out, never on one that loaded.
entries.fix: Switch off a mod you can do without, then restart.

entries.title: Over the room the game keeps for mods
where: Mods tab, when you install a ZIP
Mods tab, on the mod's row after a restart

page: This mod unpacks to 30 MB, more than the 24 MB the game keeps for mods on a phone, so it cannot be switched on here
the mods before it already fill the 96 MB the game keeps for mods

entries.meaning: All switched-on mods together can unpack to at most 96 MB, or 24 MB on a phone or low-memory device. A new mod that does not fit is installed switched off.
entries.fix: Switch off a big mod. If you made the mod, save its textures as compressed DDS and include only the ones you changed, so phone players can use it.

entries.title: Removed by the moderators
where: Mods tab, on the mod's row after a restart
Mods tab, when you install a ZIP

page: Removed by the moderators: holds art from another game. It cannot be switched on

entries.meaning: The moderators removed this version, and the reason follows the message. Every copy is switched off at the next start and cannot be switched on, even one installed from a ZIP.
entries.fix: If you installed it, remove it, or install a newer version once the author fixes it. If you made it, read the review reason, fix the problem and upload a new version. Players who update get the mod switched on again.

entries.title: The mod could not be unpacked at start
where: Mods tab, on the mod's row after a restart

page: could not be unpacked (ENOSPC)
the stored mod does not match its id
the mod list could not be written

entries.meaning: The game could not unpack this mod from browser storage when it started. The browser is usually out of memory or storage, or the stored copy is damaged.
entries.fix: Restart the game. If the message stays, remove the mod and install it again.

entries.title: timer.after before a town is loaded
where: what timer.after returns when it is refused, and the Mod log

game: load: timer.after refused: no town is loaded yet (the script's main part runs before the save loads): set it from an event

entries.meaning: A timer is kept in the mod's town store, and the main part of a script runs before the town loads. So there is nowhere to keep a timer yet.
entries.fix: Set the timer from an event, such as scene_entered or day_started.

entries.title: timer.after while the game clock is not set
where: what timer.after returns when it is refused, and the Mod log

game: day_started: timer.after refused: the game clock is not set (it reads a date before the year 2000): try again later

entries.meaning: A timer is counted in game minutes from the start of the year 2000. The game clock read a date before that, which happens only when the clock was never set. A timer set then could never come due, so it is refused and nothing is stored.
entries.fix: Nothing in the mod is wrong. Set the timer again from a later event, once the game has its date.

entries.title: Too many timers waiting
where: what timer.after returns when it is refused, and the Mod log

game: day_started: timer.after refused: this mod already has 16 timers waiting in this town

entries.meaning: A mod may have 16 timers waiting in one town.
entries.fix: Cancel one with timer.cancel, or wait for one to fire. One timer that sets the next one when it fires needs only one slot.

entries.title: The timer does not fit in the town store
where: what timer.after returns when it is refused, and the Mod log

game: day_started: timer.after refused: the timer does not fit in this mod's town store, or the store could not be written

entries.meaning: A waiting timer is kept in the mod's town store, with its name and data, and counts toward the store's 8 KB. This one would take the store over that, or the store could not be written. Nothing changed.
entries.fix: Free some room with store.set(key, nil), or give the timer shorter data.

entries.title: timer.after was called with a value it cannot use
where: what timer.after returns when it is refused, and the Mod log

game: day_started: timer.after refused: minutes must be a whole number 1 to 10080 (game minutes)
day_started: timer.after refused: name must be 1 to 40 bytes of letters, digits, _, - and .
day_started: timer.after refused: this script has no timer_fired handler (list timer_fired in scripts.events and add on("timer_fired", ...))

entries.meaning: minutes is a whole number of game minutes, 1 to 10080. name is 1 to 40 bytes of letters, digits, _, - and . only. data is text of up to 240 bytes, a number, true, false or nil. The script must also handle timer_fired, or the timer would fire to nobody.
entries.fix: Fix the call. List "timer_fired" in scripts.events and add on("timer_fired", ...) in the main part of the script.

entries.title: Script took too long
where: Mods tab, "Script stopped" on the mod's row

game: script took too long (over 200000 instructions)
script took too long (over 125 ms)
script took too long (over 250 ms)

entries.meaning: One event gets 200,000 Lua instructions per mod, and the main chunk gets the same when the game starts. Library work and memory use count towards it. That count is the same on every device, and a script that goes over it is stopped for the rest of the session, so it cannot freeze the game. "over ... ms" is the wall-clock backstop instead: 125 ms for an event run, 250 ms for the main chunk, stretched up to 8 times on a slow or busy device. Only time the count cannot see reaches it, such as one call that does a lot of work at once.
entries.fix: Do less per event. Avoid long loops and patterns like ".-.-.-" on long text, and cache results in local variables or the store. String patterns, table.sort, table.concat and memory use count towards the budget, and pcall does not get around it.

bad.text:
on("day_started", function(e)
  local n = 0
  for i = 1, 1e9 do n = n + i end
end)

entries.title: Script kept the game waiting
where: Mods tab, "Script stopped" on the mod's row

game: script kept the game waiting (3 runs in a row over 8 ms)

entries.meaning: An event run over 8 ms is a strike, and 3 strikes in a row stop the script for the session, even when each run stayed inside its instruction budget. A run under the limit clears the strikes. On a slow or busy device the limit is stretched by how slow the game itself runs there, so the number in the message can be larger than 8.
entries.fix: Do less per event. Spread work over several events, cache results in local variables or the store, and avoid long loops and patterns on long text.

entries.title: Script ran out of memory
where: Mods tab, "Script stopped" on the mod's row

game: out of memory (4 MB per mod, 16 MB for all mods together)

entries.meaning: A mod's script can use 4 MB, and all mods together 16 MB.
entries.fix: Keep fewer and smaller tables. Do not build big strings in a loop. Collect the parts and call table.concat once.

entries.title: on() with an event not in "scripts.events"
where: Mods tab, "Script stopped" on the mod's row

game: @yourname.my-mod/main.lua:1: on(): 'villager_talked' is not in this mod's "scripts.events" list in mod.json
@yourname.my-mod/main.lua:1: on(): unknown event 'tick'

entries.meaning: A script can only listen to an event that mod.json lists in "scripts.events", and the event must exist. The Events reference lists every event.
entries.fix: Add the event to "scripts.events" in mod.json, or fix its spelling in on().

entries.title: on() called from inside a handler
where: Mods tab, "Script stopped" on the mod's row

game: @yourname.my-mod/main.lua:4: on(): handlers can only be added while the script loads, not from inside a handler

entries.meaning: Handlers are added once, while main.lua first runs. A handler cannot add more handlers, and neither can a function that another mod calls with remote.call.
entries.fix: Call on() at the top level of main.lua. To change behaviour later, keep a flag in a variable.

entries.title: More than 16 handlers for one event
where: Mods tab, "Script stopped" on the mod's row

game: @yourname.my-mod/main.lua:20: on(): at most 16 handlers for 'villager_talked'

entries.meaning: A mod can add at most 16 handlers per event.
entries.fix: Use one handler that does several things.

entries.title: store.set before a town is loaded
where: Mods tab, "Script stopped" on the mod's row

game: @yourname.my-mod/main.lua:3: store.set: no town is loaded yet (the script's main part runs before the save loads): save from an event, or use store.client

entries.meaning: "store" is kept per town, and the main part of a script runs before the town loads. So store.set is refused there and store.get returns nil.
entries.fix: Save from an event such as day_started or villager_talked. For data that belongs to the browser and not the town, use store.client.

entries.title: store.player.set with no player in the game
where: Mods tab, "Script stopped" on the mod's row

game: @yourname.my-mod/main.lua:8: store.player.set: no player is in the game yet (game.player() is nil): save once a player is in the town, or use store for the town's own data

entries.meaning: "store.player" is kept per resident. It needs a resident in the game: game.player() names them. Every event of a town has one, day_started at boot included. When game.player() is nil, store.player.set has no one to save for and store.player.get returns nil.
entries.fix: Check game.player() first. For data that belongs to the whole town, use store.

entries.title: remote.add of a name "exports" does not list
where: Mods tab, "Script stopped" on the mod's row

game: @yourname.my-lib/main.lua:3: remote.add: count is not in mod.json "exports" (a library offers what it lists)

entries.meaning: Your mod.json has "exports", so remote.add offers only the names it lists.
entries.fix: Add the name to "exports" with a one-line description, or offer one that is listed.

entries.title: remote.add or remote.call refused
where: Mods tab, "Script stopped" on the mod's row

game: @yourname.my-mod/main.lua:4: remote.call: tea.lib offers no function brew
@yourname.my-mod/main.lua:4: remote.call: tea.lib is already running (a call back into it would be a cycle), refused
@yourname.my-mod/main.lua:1: remote.add: functions can only be offered while the script loads
@yourname.my-mod/main.lua:6: remote.call: tea.lib has not updated this town's data yet (its data_migrated runs after this one), refused

entries.meaning: A remote.add or remote.call was refused. The text after the function name says why.
entries.fix: For remote.add, offer the function while the script loads, under a name of a-z, 0-9 and _ up to 32 characters. For remote.call, check with remote.has that the mod is on and offers the name. Pass only nil, booleans, numbers, strings and tables of them, up to 64 KB and 16 levels deep. Do not call back into a mod that is already running. In data_migrated, change only your own data and call other mods from a later event.

entries.title: store.set refused a value
where: Mods tab, "Script stopped" on the mod's row

game: @yourname.my-mod/main.lua:3: store.set: only strings, numbers and booleans can be saved
@yourname.my-mod/main.lua:3: store.set: the store would be over 8192 bytes, nothing was saved
@yourname.my-mod/main.lua:3: store.set: key longer than 64 bytes
@yourname.my-mod/main.lua:3: store.set: a key cannot start with a control character
@yourname.my-mod/main.lua:3: store.player.set: only strings, numbers and booleans can be saved

entries.meaning: store.set refused the value, so nothing was saved. The error stops the script unless you wrap the call in pcall.
entries.fix: Save only strings, numbers and booleans. Keep a key to 64 bytes and a value to 1024 bytes, with no zero bytes, no NaN and no control character at the start of a key. A mod has 8 KB per town, shared by store and store.player, and 8 KB per browser in store.client. To save a table, turn it into a string such as "3,7,12".

entries.title: Something scripts may not do
where: Mods tab, "Script stopped" on the mod's row

game: @yourname.my-mod/main.lua:2: setmetatable: __gc is not allowed in mod scripts (finalizers cannot be stopped)
@yourname.my-mod/main.lua:5: tables with a __len metamethod are not supported here in mod scripts
@yourname.my-mod/main.lua:4: math.random is not available: use rng() (seeded, so a reload cannot reroll)
@yourname.my-mod/main.lua:1: math.randomseed is not available: use rng() (seeded, so a reload cannot reroll)

entries.meaning: The script used a Lua feature that mod scripts do not have. __gc finalizers, and __len metamethods on a table passed to table.insert, remove, sort or concat, are switched off, and math.random and math.randomseed raise an error.
entries.fix: Remove the metamethod and use plain tables. Write rng() for math.random(), rng(n) for math.random(n) and rng(m, n) for math.random(m, n). rng() is seeded by the mod, the town and the game day, so a reload cannot reroll a result. io, os, load, require, dofile and debug do not exist.

entries.title: The script could not keep running
where: Mods tab, "Script stopped" on the mod's row

game: the script's Lua state failed and was dropped
the script raised an error that is not a string

entries.meaning: The script failed in a way the game cannot recover from, or it raised an error with error({...}) instead of a string.
entries.fix: Raise errors with error("text"). If the message says the state failed, report it with the mod, because that is a bug in the game.

entries.title: A Lua syntax error
where: Mods tab, "Script stopped" on the mod's row
the check tool (playac-mod check)

page: main.lua:4: unfinished string near '"hello'
main.lua:7: ')' expected near 'log'
main.lua:2: <name> expected near '='
main.lua:9: break outside a loop at line 9
main.lua:3: no visible label 'done' for goto at line 3
main.lua:6: attempt to assign to const variable 'limit'
game: @yourname.my-mod/main.lua:5: 'end' expected (to close 'function' at line 2) near <eof>
@yourname.my-mod/main.lua:3: unexpected symbol near '='

entries.meaning: The script is not valid Lua 5.4, so it never starts and none of its handlers run. The Mods tab shows the file, the line and what Lua expected there, and the rest of the mod still works.
entries.fix: Open the file at the line shown, which is often just after the real mistake. The usual causes are a missing `end`, `then` or `do`, a string with no closing quote, `!=` where Lua writes `~=`, and `+` where Lua joins strings with `..`. `playac-mod check` finds the same error before you install.

entries.title: The script raised an error
where: Mods tab, "Script stopped" on the mod's row

game: @yourname.my-mod/main.lua:7: attempt to index a nil value (global 'io')
@yourname.my-mod/main.lua:3: attempt to call a nil value (global 'give_item')

entries.meaning: Your script raised a Lua error, and the text gives the file and line. The script is stopped for the rest of the session, and the rest of the mod keeps working.
entries.fix: Open the file at the line shown and fix it, then reinstall and restart. The usual causes are a typo in a name, a call to something the API does not have, and indexing nil. Use log() to print values, and pcall around code that may fail.

entries.title: A command not in "permissions"
where: what cmd.<name> returns when a command is refused, the command_finished event and the Mod log

game: give_item is not in this mod's "permissions" in mod.json

entries.meaning: A script may only use the commands that "permissions" in mod.json lists. Players see that list on the Mods tab.
entries.fix: Add the command to "permissions", or stop calling it. Trying again does not help, because the list is read when the game starts.

entries.title: Too many commands in one event
where: what cmd.<name> returns when a command is refused, the command_finished event and the Mod log

game: send_letter: at most 4 commands in one event

entries.meaning: A mod may queue at most 4 commands while one event runs.
entries.fix: Queue fewer commands per event. The count starts again at the next event, so the rest can go then.

entries.title: The command queue is full
where: what cmd.<name> returns when a command is refused, the command_finished event and the Mod log

game: show_line: this mod already has 8 commands waiting
ask: the game's command queue is full (32), try later

entries.meaning: Commands wait in a queue until the game applies them at the end of a frame. At most 8 of one mod's commands wait at once, and 32 for all mods together.
entries.fix: Try again from a later event. The queue empties as the game applies it.

entries.title: The day's cap for this command is used up
where: what cmd.<name> returns when a command is refused, the command_finished event and the Mod log

game: send_letter: at most 3 a day for each mod
take_bells: at most 6 a day for each mod

entries.meaning: Each game day in each town, a mod may send 3 letters, give 5 items, show 20 lines and ask 10 questions. It may also ask for items 6 times and for Bells 6 times. A take counts when its question is shown, whatever the player answers. The caps are per town, not per player, and a reload does not reset them.
entries.fix: Try again on the next game day. Remember in the store what you already sent today, so the script does not ask again.

entries.title: An item a command cannot hand out
where: what cmd.<name> returns when a command is refused, the command_finished event and the Mod log

game: give_item: item 0x2100 is money
send_letter: item 0xF000 is not an item or furniture the game has
give_item: a mod can only give its own new items, by "<this mod's id>:<item id>"
give_item: no item by that id in this mod's items file
take_item: item 0x2503 is a villager's errand item
take_item: a mod can only take its own new items, by "<this mod's id>:<item id>"
the item is not this town's to give (its mod is off, or this is not your town)
the letter is gone (its mod's letters file did not load)

entries.meaning: Items follow the shop's rules, so a command cannot hand out money, turnips, tickets, grab bags, fossils or reserved numbers. take_item follows the same rules, and never takes the goods of a villager's errand. An item is "0x" and four hex digits, or one of this mod's own new items by its full id. A letter id must be one in this mod's own letters file. The last two messages come in command_finished, when the game applies the command. They mean the mod's item or letter was there at the call and gone when the game applied the command, because its mod was switched off, its file did not load or the town is not yours.
entries.fix: Pick another item. Write it as "0x2800" or "yourname.my-mod:thing". An item that is not a number or one of those forms is command-args instead.

entries.title: A command's arguments are wrong
where: what cmd.<name> returns when a command is refused, the command_finished event and the Mod log

game: send_letter: text must be 1 to 192 characters
send_letter: the text does not fit a letter (6 lines)
ask: choices must be a list of 2 to 4 answers
show_line: text must be 1 to 400 bytes
take_item: count must be a whole number 1 to 15
take_bells: amount must be a whole number 1 to 99999
take_bells: takes a table: { amount = ... }
give_item: item must be an item number, "0x" and four hex digits, or this mod's "author.mod:thing"
send_letter: item must be an item number or "0x" and four hex digits
set_shop_goods: goods must list 1 to the goods the shop takes
set_shop_open: open must be true, false or nil

entries.meaning: The command was called with a value it cannot use.
entries.fix: Check the call against the reference (/modding/reference/) and shorten the text. A letter is 1 to 192 characters in 6 lines, with "from" up to 8 characters and paper 0 to 63. A line is up to 400 bytes. A question is up to 120 characters, with 2 to 4 answers of up to 16 characters.

entries.title: Commands are off in The City
where: what cmd.<name> returns when a command is refused, the command_finished event and the Mod log

game: commands are switched off in The City
send_letter: commands are switched off in The City
set_shop_open: shops are off in The City

entries.meaning: In The City every command is refused, because other players there do not have your mod. A refused command does not count against the daily caps.
entries.fix: Nothing to fix. Handle the nil return or the failed command_finished, and try again at home, for example from scene_entered.

entries.title: A client setting cannot decide what the town gets
where: what cmd.<name> returns when a command is refused, the command_finished event and the Mod log

game: give_item: this event read the client setting "gift", and a client setting cannot decide what the town gets (make it a world setting)

entries.meaning: A setting whose "scope" is "client" is the player's own. It may decide only what that player sees or hears. In an event that read one with settings.get, cmd.send_letter, cmd.give_item, cmd.take_item and cmd.take_bells are refused, because they change what the town or the player has.
entries.fix: If the setting decides what a letter says, what is given or taken, or when, take "scope": "client" off it: it is then a world setting, and a friend who visits runs the host's value. If it only decides what the player sees, read it in the event that shows the line, not in the one that sends, gives or takes. Trying again does not help.

entries.title: A shop command the shop cannot take
where: what cmd.<name> returns when a command is refused, the command_finished event and the Mod log

game: set_shop_goods: there is no such shop
set_shop_open: Crazy Redd's tent has no open
set_shop_goods: Able Sisters has no goods
set_shop_goods: a later mod changes Nook's store: bean.night-shop
set_shop_open: a shop changes what visitors see, so the mod needs "scope": "world"

entries.meaning: cmd.set_shop_goods and cmd.set_shop_open change one shop, by its id in the shop table, for the rest of the game day. They are refused when the id is not in the table, when the shop has no goods (set_shop_goods) or no open (set_shop_open) in the table, when a mod later in the load order changes that shop (it has the shop whole), and in a mod without "scope": "world". The refusal comes at the call: the command returns nil, this message and this code.
entries.fix: Use a shop id from the shop table (/modding/guides/shops/#table) that has the field. If a later mod has the shop, the player decides the order in the Mods tab. Trying again does not help.

entries.title: A mod this one can use is not there
where: what remote.version returns, and remote.call for an optional dependency

game: yourname.weather is not loaded
yourname.weather is loaded, but it has no running script

entries.meaning: The mod is named in "depends" or "optional_depends", and it is not installed, is switched off, did not load, or has no running script. This is not an error. remote.version returns nil, this message and this code, and remote.call to an optional dependency returns the same three without calling anything.
entries.fix: Nothing to fix. Do what the mod does on its own when the code comes back.

entries.title: A mod this one can use is another version
where: what remote.version returns, and remote.call for an optional dependency

game: yourname.weather is loaded, but its version is outside the range this mod names

entries.meaning: The mod loaded, but its version is not inside the range "optional_depends" gives for it, so it counts as absent. A needed dependency outside its range stops the mod from loading instead.
entries.fix: Widen the range in mod.json if your mod works with that version. Otherwise do what the mod does on its own.

entries.title: remote.version asked about a mod mod.json does not name
where: what remote.version returns, and remote.call for an optional dependency

game: yourname.weather is not in this mod's "depends" or "optional_depends"

entries.meaning: remote.version answers only for the mods this mod names in "depends" or "optional_depends".
entries.fix: Add the mod to "optional_depends" in mod.json, with the range of versions your script works with.

entries.title: Only the town's owner changes a town
where: what cmd.<name> returns when a command is refused, the command_finished event and the Mod log

game: only the town owner's game can change the town (you are visiting)
give_item: only the town owner's game can change the town (you are visiting)

entries.meaning: On a visit, send_letter, give_item, take_item and take_bells are refused, because only the town owner's game changes a town or a save. They do not count against the daily caps, and show_line and ask still work.
entries.fix: Nothing to fix. Handle the nil return or the failed command_finished, and send it once the player is home.

entries.title: A lent mod acts only in its town
where: what cmd.<name> returns when a command is refused, the command_finished event and the Mod log

game: a friend's mod lent for a visit acts only in their town

entries.meaning: This mod was lent to a visitor for one visit. At the visitor's home its commands are refused and its shop, Nook goods, board notices, items and renames do nothing, so it never changes the visitor's own town or save. The game refuses the command when it applies it, not at the call. So cmd.<name> returns an id, and this code arrives in command_finished.
entries.fix: Nothing to fix. Your mod runs normally for players who installed it.

entries.title: No room for a letter or an item
where: what cmd.<name> returns when a command is refused, the command_finished event and the Mod log

game: the mailbox and the post office are both full
the pockets, the mailbox and the post office are all full
the pockets are full (a new item cannot come by mail)

entries.meaning: There was no room for the letter or the item. One of the game's items can go to the pockets or come by mail, and one of the mod's own new items can only go to the pockets.
entries.fix: Try again later, from a later event and not in a loop. A command refused for no room still counts against the day's cap, because it reached the game. Three letters refused for a full mailbox use up the day's letters, and the next one is command-day-cap.

entries.title: A line or a question could not be drawn
where: what cmd.<name> returns when a command is refused, the command_finished event and the Mod log

game: the text cannot be drawn in the window (too many pages?)

entries.meaning: The game could not draw the line or the question in the window, because the text has too many pages. It arrives in command_finished. The command still counts against the day's cap, because it reached the game.
entries.fix: Shorten the text. Trying the same command again does not help.

entries.title: The player does not hold what a take asks for
where: what cmd.<name> returns when a command is refused, the command_finished event and the Mod log

game: take_item: the pockets do not hold 3 of that item in plain slots
take_bells: the wallet holds fewer than 500 Bells
the wallet no longer holds that many Bells

entries.meaning: take_item counts only plain pocket slots. A wrapped present, an item held for a villager's errand and a mod item standing on the same piece do not count. take_bells reads the wallet only, never the bank or a money bag. When the player holds less than the take asks for, nothing is asked and nothing is taken. It does not count against the daily cap.
entries.fix: Check game.pockets() or game.bells() first, and tell the player what to bring with cmd.show_line. Try again from a later event.

good.text: if (game.bells() or 0) >= 500 then cmd.take_bells{ amount = 500 } end

entries.title: The player said no to a take
where: what cmd.<name> returns when a command is refused, the command_finished event and the Mod log

game: the player said no, nothing was taken

entries.meaning: Before take_item or take_bells takes anything, the game asks the player in its own words, with the true item, count or amount. The player answered no, or closed the window with no pick. Nothing was taken. The question still counts against the daily cap, so a mod cannot ask again and again.
entries.fix: Nothing to fix. Carry on without the item or the Bells, and do not ask again in the same event.

entries.title: The name has a word the site does not allow
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: The mod's name has a word the site does not allow. Pick another name.

entries.meaning: The mod list is public, so a mod's name goes through the site's word filter.
entries.fix: Change "name" in mod.json, raise the version and upload again.

entries.title: An author name has a word the site does not allow
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: An author name has a word the site does not allow. Use another name.

entries.meaning: Author names show on the mod list, so they go through the site's word filter.
entries.fix: Change the name in "authors" in mod.json, raise the version and upload again.

entries.title: A text file is not text
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: "notes.txt" is not text. A .txt, .md or .lua file must be plain UTF-8 text.

entries.meaning: A reviewer reads every .txt, .md and .lua file of a shared mod, and the site's word filter reads them too. So each one must be plain text: UTF-8, with no zero byte. A picture, an archive or any other data under a text name is refused. A file saved as UTF-16 is refused as well.
entries.fix: Save the file as UTF-8 in your editor. Take out a file that is not text, or give a picture its real .png or .dds name.

entries.title: A line ends with a lone carriage return
where: Mods tab, when you install a ZIP
the check tool (playac-mod check)
Share a mod, when you upload

page: "main.lua" has a carriage return with no line feed after it. Save it with LF or CRLF line endings
"en.json" has a carriage return with no line feed after it. Save it with LF or CRLF line endings
registry: "main.lua" has a carriage return with no line feed after it. Save it with LF or CRLF line endings.

entries.meaning: Lua ends a line at a carriage return (CR) on its own, but the review shows a file broken at line feeds (LF) only. Code after a lone CR would look like part of the line before it, a comment for example, while the game runs it. So a mod's .lua and .json files must end lines with LF or CRLF. The Mods tab, playac-mod check and the mod list all refuse it.
entries.fix: Set your editor to LF (or CRLF) line endings and save the file again. Old Mac editors write CR alone.

entries.title: The mod carries too much text
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: The text files of the mod add up to more than 4 MB. A mod may carry at most that much text.

entries.meaning: The .json, .lua, .txt and .md files of a shared mod can be at most 4 MB together. The site's word filter reads all of it at upload and a reviewer may have to read it. An upload whose text takes the filter too long to read is refused with the same words.
entries.fix: Take out text the mod does not need, such as generated lists or logs. Split the mod in two when all of it is needed.

entries.title: Sign in to share
where: Share a mod, when you upload

site: Sign in to share a mod.

entries.meaning: Sharing a mod needs an account.
entries.fix: Sign in, then upload again.

entries.title: Accept the mod rules first
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: Confirm your age and accept the mod rules before you share a mod.

entries.meaning: The first time you share, you give your age and accept the mod rules.
entries.fix: Answer the questions above the upload button, then upload again.

entries.title: Sharing is for players 13 or older
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: Sharing mods is for players 13 or older.

entries.meaning: Players under 13 can make and install mods but cannot share them.
entries.fix: Keep the mod for yourself, or ask a parent or guardian to share it from their own account.

entries.title: This account cannot share mods
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: Mod uploads are switched off for your account.

entries.meaning: This account cannot share mods. Its mods were removed for copyright several times, or a moderator switched uploads off for it.
entries.fix: Read the mod rules page for how to appeal.

entries.title: This version is already uploaded
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: This version of the mod is already uploaded: a version is never replaced, and its number is not used again, even after it is removed (only a rejected version's number is free again). Raise the version in mod.json.

entries.meaning: Every upload is a new version, and a version is never replaced, so everyone who has it has the same files. A version number is used once, even after the version is removed, unless a moderator refused it.
entries.fix: Raise "version" in mod.json (1.0.0 to 1.0.1) and upload again.

entries.title: A screenshot is needed, or one could not be read
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: Add at least one screenshot of the mod in the game (PNG or JPEG). It is shown on the mod's page.
Screenshot 1 must be a PNG or a JPEG.
Screenshot 1 must be 200 to 4096 pixels a side.
Screenshot 1 is larger than a 4K screen (3840 by 2160 pixels). Make it smaller.
Screenshot 1 is a 16 bit PNG. Save it as an ordinary (8 bit) PNG or a JPEG.
Screenshot 1 is a progressive JPEG larger than 1920 by 1080 pixels. Save it as a standard (baseline) JPEG or a PNG, or make it smaller.
Screenshot 1 could not be read: is it a whole PNG or JPEG?
Each screenshot must be at most 2 MB.
Send at most 4 screenshots.

entries.meaning: Every shared version needs 1 to 4 screenshots of the mod in the game, and one was missing or could not be used. The site saves them again, so no hidden photo data survives.
entries.fix: Add a screenshot in Share a mod, or in .playac/screenshots/, which a GitHub import reads. Use a PNG or JPEG of 200 to 4096 pixels a side, at most 3840 by 2160 pixels in all and 2 MB. Save it as an ordinary 8-bit PNG or a standard JPEG, not a 16-bit PNG or a progressive JPEG over 1920 by 1080.

entries.title: The changelog line could not be used
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: The changelog line must be at most 300 characters of text, with at most 4 line breaks.
The changelog line has a word the site does not allow. Say it another way.
Send one changelog line.

entries.meaning: A shared version may carry one optional line on what it changes. The line that came with this one could not be used.
entries.fix: Shorten the line in Share a mod, or in this version's section of CHANGELOG.md, or leave it out. Keep it to 300 characters and 4 line breaks. It goes through the site's word filter.

entries.title: The upload form could not be read
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: The upload form has no zip.
The upload form could not be read.
The upload form has a part this site does not read.
The upload form has no boundary.
Send one zip at a time.

entries.meaning: An upload is a form with the ZIP, the screenshots and an optional changelog line. This one was not sent the way the site sends it.
entries.fix: Share from Settings, Mods. A script of your own must send multipart/form-data with the parts zip, screenshot and changelog.

entries.title: Another player owns this id
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: Another player already uploaded a mod with this id. Pick a different id.

entries.meaning: A mod id belongs to the account that first shared it.
entries.fix: Change "id" in mod.json, with your own name before the dot.

entries.title: Too many uploads
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: You can upload 5 mods an hour. Try again later.
You have 10 uploads waiting for review. Upload more once some are reviewed.

entries.meaning: There is a limit on uploads per hour and on uploads waiting for review.
entries.fix: Wait for a review, or try again in an hour. Test on your own computer first, so each upload counts.

entries.title: Your shared mods use all your space
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: Your mods would take more than 64 MB. Ask for an old version to be taken down, or make this one smaller.

entries.meaning: Each account has a total size for all its shared versions, and this upload would go over it.
entries.fix: Ask for an old version to be removed, or make the mod smaller.

entries.title: Upload busy or too slow
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: Another upload from your account or your network is still going, or the server is busy. Try again in a minute.
Your connection was too slow to upload the zip. Try again on a better connection.

entries.meaning: Only one upload runs at a time per account and network, and the file has to keep arriving.
entries.fix: Wait a minute and try again, on a steadier connection if it was too slow.

entries.title: The images could not be checked
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: We couldn't check the images in your mod just now. Nothing was uploaded. Try again in a few minutes.

entries.meaning: Every image is checked before an upload is accepted, and the check did not answer. Nothing was uploaded.
entries.fix: Try again in a few minutes.

entries.title: The upload was refused
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: This upload can't be accepted.

entries.meaning: The upload was refused without a reason being given, or the account cannot share right now.
entries.fix: Read the mod rules. If you think it is a mistake, contact the moderators.

entries.title: Sharing mods is not open
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: Sharing mods is not open yet. Mods you install from a ZIP file still work.

entries.meaning: Sharing mods is not open, so uploads and GitHub imports are refused. Installing a mod from a ZIP still works.
entries.fix: Keep making and testing the mod on your own computer, and share it once sharing opens.

entries.title: Uploads are paused while reviews catch up
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: New mod uploads are paused while the review queue catches up. Nothing was uploaded. Try again in a few days.

entries.meaning: When the oldest upload has waited more than a week for review, new uploads and imports stop until the queue is shorter. Nothing was uploaded.
entries.fix: Try again in a few days.

entries.title: Two-factor sign-in is needed
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: Turn on two-factor sign-in on your Profile page before you share a mod.
Enter the code from your authenticator app to share a mod.
Enter the code from your authenticator app to approve playac-mod.
Sharing mods is switched off on this server for now.
Too many wrong codes in a row, so code checks are paused for a while. Wait, then try again with a fresh code. If the account logs in with an email address, we emailed it.
That code is not right, or it was used already. Wait for the next one and try again.

entries.meaning: Sharing a mod and importing one from GitHub both need two-factor sign-in and a recent code from your authenticator app. A code works once. After 5 wrong codes in a row, code checks pause for a minute or longer, and we email the account if it logs in with an email address.
entries.fix: Switch on two-factor sign-in on your Profile page, then enter a code from your authenticator app when asked. If codes are paused, wait, check that the phone's clock is right and use a fresh code.

entries.title: The name before the dot is another player's
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: The part of the id before the dot belongs to another player's account. Use your own name before the dot.

entries.meaning: The part of a mod id before the dot belongs to the account that first uploaded under it, even while that upload waits for review. In kim.tea-stall that part is kim. It is free again only if every upload under it was refused.
entries.fix: Change "id" in mod.json to start with your own name.

entries.title: These files were removed from the mod list
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: These files were removed from the mod list, so they can't be shared again.
site: These files were removed from the mod list, so they can't be shared again.

entries.meaning: These are the same files as a version the moderators removed. They cannot be shared again under any id or version.
entries.fix: Read the review decision on the removed version and change what it named. If you think the removal was wrong, see the mod rules page.

entries.title: Too many upload attempts
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: You can try 12 uploads an hour. Try again later.

entries.meaning: Every upload attempt counts towards the hourly limit, refused ones too, because each one costs a check of every image.
entries.fix: Run `playac-mod check` first, then try again in an hour.

entries.title: Too many or too large pictures
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: Your mod has more than 500 different pictures. Split it into smaller mods.
Your mod's pictures add up to more than 67 million pixels, or are too slow to check. Split it into smaller mods.

entries.meaning: One upload may hold at most 500 different pictures and about 67 million pixels in all, which is 16 textures of 2048 by 2048. The same file used many times counts once.
entries.fix: Split the mod into smaller mods, or make the large textures smaller.

entries.title: Not a GitHub repository and tag
where: Share a mod, when you upload

registry: Write it as github.com/<owner>/<repo>@<tag>, for example github.com/you/tea-stall@v1.2.0.
That is not a GitHub owner and repository name.

entries.meaning: Import from GitHub takes a public repository and one of its tags.
entries.fix: Write github.com/you/your-repo@v1.2.0, with a tag that exists on GitHub.

entries.title: That change to the version is not allowed now
where: the Mods tab

registry: A moderator took this version out of the list. Upload a fixed version, or ask the moderators to look again.
The moderators are looking at this version, so it can't be listed again for now.
Another decision on this version came first. Reload and look again.

entries.meaning: The version's state does not allow that change. Only a moderator can list again a version that a moderator withdrew, and a decision made first wins. A version the moderators are looking at cannot be listed again until they decide.
entries.fix: Reload the Mods tab. If a moderator withdrew the version, read the reason, fix the mod and upload a new version. If the moderators are looking at it, wait for their decision.

entries.title: Update available
where: Mods tab, on the mod's row after a restart

site: Update available

entries.meaning: A newer listed version of the mod is in the mod list.
entries.fix: Open Browse mods, install the update and restart.

entries.title: Withdrawn from the mod list
where: Mods tab, on the mod's row after a restart

site: This version was withdrawn from the mod list. It still works.

entries.meaning: The author or a moderator withdrew this version. It still works and friends who both have it can still visit, but new players cannot install it.
entries.fix: Nothing to do. If the author shares a newer version, update to it.

entries.title: Mods are switched off for everyone
where: the Mods tab

registry: Mods are switched off for everyone for now while we fix a problem. Your mods are still installed and come back on their own.

entries.meaning: We switched mods off for everyone for a while. Games start without mods and no mod can be downloaded, but nothing is uninstalled.
entries.fix: Nothing to do. Your mods come back on their own.

entries.title: The two towns run different World mods
where: the Multiplayer panel, when a visit is refused

site: Your World mods don't match. Visits need the same World mods (the ones visitors can see) in both towns (or none). Change them in Settings, Mods.
Kim's town runs Tea Stall 1.2.0, you don't. Visits need the same World mods (the ones visitors can see) in both towns. Change them in Settings, Mods.

entries.meaning: A friend visit starts only when both towns run the same World mods that count for visits, in the same versions and order. The message names what differs.
entries.fix: Make the World mods match in Settings, Mods, or switch them off and restart. A World mod counts when it has "textures", "shops" or "items" content, and a Just you mod never counts. See the multiplayer guide for the full rule (https://playaconline.com/modding/guides/multiplayer/).

entries.title: A friend's mods could not be loaded for the visit
where: the Multiplayer panel, when a visit is refused

page: the download for bean.tea-stall 1.2.0 does not match the friend's copy
the download for bean.tea-stall 1.2.0 is a different mod
the friend's mods do not add up to their town's mod set
the friend's settings for bean.tea-stall are not ones that mod takes
registry: Invalid mod list: the mod list does not match the mod set hash.
site: Couldn't load Kim's mods for this visit. Couldn't download Tea Stall: the mod list answered 404.

entries.meaning: You agreed to visit with your friend's mods, and one could not be downloaded, did not match your friend's version or had settings the mod does not take. Nothing was kept or installed, and the visit was left.
entries.fix: Ask again later. If it keeps happening, the mod may have been removed or updated. Both players can then install the same version from Browse mods.

entries.title: A City mod was refused
where: the Multiplayer panel, when a visit is refused

page: bean.lamps: a City mod may only hold textures and lines, not shops
bean.lamps: a City mod may not run scripts

entries.meaning: The City's own mods may only change textures and lines. A mod with a shop, a script or commands is never loaded there.

entries.title: Nintendo or other franchise content
where: the review decision on your upload
entries.meaning: The mod holds art, textures, models, music, sound or text taken from a Nintendo game or another game, film, show or brand, or redrawn copies of them. Mods here may only hold work you made yourself.
entries.fix: Replace every taken file with art you made yourself, then upload a new version. Redrawn copies of Nintendo art count as taken.

entries.title: Nintendo or franchise names or logos
where: the review decision on your upload
entries.meaning: The mod's name, id, description or pictures use Nintendo's names or logos, or another brand's, in a way that could make it look official. Give your mod its own name.
entries.fix: Rename the mod and its id, and remove logos from pictures. "AC" or "Animal Crossing" in a name can make it look official.

entries.title: Someone else's work
where: the review decision on your upload
entries.meaning: The mod holds work made by someone else, such as another modder's files, without their permission. Share only what you made, or what you have written permission to share.
entries.fix: Remove the other person's files, or get their written permission and say so in the description.

entries.title: Removed after a copyright notice
where: the review decision on your upload
entries.meaning: The owner of a copyright sent us a notice saying this mod copies their work, so it was removed. If you believe the notice is a mistake, the mod rules page says how to respond.
entries.fix: If you believe the notice is wrong, send a counter-notice. The mod rules page explains how.

entries.title: Sexual content
where: the review decision on your upload
entries.meaning: The mod holds sexual or sexually suggestive pictures or text. Players of every age use this site.
entries.fix: Remove it. Mods here are for players of every age.

entries.title: Gore or graphic violence
where: the review decision on your upload
entries.meaning: The mod holds gore, graphic violence or disturbing pictures or text. Players of every age use this site.
entries.fix: Remove it. Mods here are for players of every age.

entries.title: Hate or harassment
where: the review decision on your upload
entries.meaning: The mod attacks or demeans people for who they are, or targets a real person to harass them.
entries.fix: Remove it.

entries.title: Personal information
where: the review decision on your upload
entries.meaning: The mod holds someone's personal information, such as a real name with an address, a phone number, an email address or a photo of a real person.
entries.fix: Remove any real names with addresses, phone numbers, emails or photos of real people.

entries.title: Harmful script
where: the review decision on your upload
entries.meaning: The mod's script is made to break the game, slow it down on purpose, flood players with messages, or get around the limits mods run under.
entries.fix: Make the script do only what the description says, inside the limits. Do not try to get around the budget.

entries.title: Misleading
where: the review decision on your upload
entries.meaning: The mod's name, description or pictures do not match what it does, or it pretends to come from someone else.
entries.fix: Make the name, description and pictures match what the mod does.

entries.title: Does not work
where: the review decision on your upload
entries.meaning: The mod does not load or does not do what it says. Fix it and upload it again.
entries.fix: Test it with `playac-mod check`, then in the game with developer mode and the Mod log. Fix it and upload a higher version.

entries.title: Spam or duplicate
where: the review decision on your upload
entries.meaning: The mod repeats another upload, or is an advert or a placeholder rather than a mod.
entries.fix: Share each mod once, and only finished mods.

entries.title: Upload rights removed
where: the review decision on your upload
entries.meaning: Mods from this account were removed for copyright several times, so under the repeat-infringer policy on the mod rules page its mods are no longer shared.
entries.fix: Read the mod rules page for how to appeal.

entries.title: Removed at your request
where: the review decision on your upload
entries.meaning: You asked for this version to be removed.
entries.fix: Nothing to do.

entries.title: Another rule
where: the review decision on your upload
entries.meaning: The mod breaks another of the mod rules. The moderator's note says which.
entries.fix: Read the moderator's note. It says which rule.
